prompt: Which design correctly uses composition to give a Robot a Speaker?
choices: class Robot extends Speaker { void speak() { say("Hi"); } }
class Robot { private Speaker speaker; Robot(Speaker s) { speaker = s; } void speak() { speaker.say("Hi"); } }
class Robot { static Speaker speaker = new Speaker(); }
class Robot implements Speaker { void say(String s) {} }
explanation: Option B injects a Speaker via the constructor (dependency injection) and delegates say() to it. Option A uses inheritance (is-a, not has-a). Option C uses a static field (global state, not composition). Option D implements Speaker (makes Robot a Speaker, not a has-a relationship).
